design_name: INFEASIBLE AS STATED (3rd attempt) - open-system substitute: Termite-mound-inspired ground-coupled pre-heating surface
inspiration_source: Macrotermes termite mound: soil-coupled galleries that exchange heat with deeper, thermally stable ground; the stated request has no valid analog
physical_mechanism: FEASIBILITY NOTE: Both previous concepts failed solely because the request violates the first law of thermodynamics (net heat output from a closed, adiabatic system without energy input, efficiency > 300 %). This cannot be fixed by any new concept; a third, fourth or n-th bionic idea will fail for the same reason, and the honest answer to the user is that the requested device cannot exist. As a physically valid, energy-conserving alternative: a termite-mound-like gallery surface coupled to the ground draws geothermal heat (open system; the ground is the energy source) to pre-heat ventilation air or a heat-pump brine. Modeled: steady 1D conduction through a soil layer between deep ground and the exchanger surface, d2T/dx2 = 0, with fixed temperatures at both ends. Delivered heat equals heat drawn from the ground; efficiency is <= 100 % with respect to that source.
